<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par121 />{{GHGmargin-letter|121|b}}
Other examples are: after Niph., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּוָּלֵד לַֽחֲנוֹךְ אֶת־עִירָד|translate=and unto Enoch was born Irad}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=26|verse=60}}, and after an infinitive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=5}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=8|hidebook=1}} (after an infinitive); 29:27 (unless {{GHGheb|text=וְנִתְּנָה}} is 1st plur. cohortative); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=28|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=6|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=7|verse=10}} (after an infinitive); 26:55 (cf. verse 53); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=20|verse=8}} (where, however, for {{GHGheb|text=יִמַּס}} the Hiph. {{GHGheb|text=יַמֵּס}} should be read, according to 1:28); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=10}}; with the object preceding, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=2|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=24}}.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=30}} {{GHGheb|text=יִנָּתֵן}} is to be read or {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}} is to be omitted, as in the parallel passage {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=15}}.</ref>— Also after Puʿal, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=20}}; ''before'' Puʿal, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=3}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} equivalent to the internal object {{GHGheb|text=עֲבֹדָה}}=''which they have caused to be served by thee''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=9}}; according to the Masoretic text also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=22}}, where, however, the Samaritan and LXX read {{GHGheb|text=יָֽלְדָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=יֻלַּד}}; the Samaritan in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=26}} and 46:27 also reads {{GHGheb|text=יָֽלְדוּ}}, and this (or {{GHGheb|text=יֻלַּד}}) should certainly be read instead of {{GHGheb|text=יֻלְדוּ}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=22}}.—After Hoph., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=27|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=10|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=16|verse=27|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=16|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=15}}; after the infinitive Hoph., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}} f., 27:7; ''before'' Hoph., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=13|verse=6}}; after the infinitive ''Hothpaʿel'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=55}} f.

{{GHGmargin-letter|121|c}}
'''2.''' Verbs which in the active take two accusatives ({{GHGpar|117|cc}}) retain in the passive construction at least ''one'' accusative, namely that of the second or remoter object, whilst the nearer object now becomes the subject. Thus, corresponding to {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶ֫ךָּ|translate=which I will show thee}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=1}}) the passive is {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה מָרְאֶה}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=40}}) ''which thou hast been shown'', i.e. which has been shown to thee; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=30}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=49}} with an accusative of the person); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=3}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=מֻדְבָּק מַלְקוֹחָ֑י}} depends on an assumed transitive {{GHGheb|text=הִדְבִּיק}} governing two accusatives (= ''my tongue is made to cleave to my jaws''); also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=20}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֶ֫רֶב תְּאֻכְּלוּ|translate=ye shall be devoured with the sword}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֶרֶב}} is not an ''accus. instrumenti'', but most probably an accusative of the object retained from the active construction.<ref>In the active, the sentence would be ''I will cause the sword to devour you''; by the rule stated above, under ''c'', this would become in the passive, ''the sword'' (nom.) ''shall be made to devour you'' (acc.). Instead of this, the remoter object is here made the subject, and the nearer object is retained in the accusative. Otherwise, the only possible explanation would be, according to the Arabic idiom, ''to cause one to devour the sword'' (remoter object), i.e. to give him over to it. It would then be simplest to read {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽאכְלוּ}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|121|d}}
Rem. 1. Examples of the retention of the second accusative are—(''a'') with {{GHGterm|verba induendi}} and ''exuendi'' ({{GHGpar|117|cc}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּסּוּ הָרִים צִלָּהּ|translate=the mountains were covered with the shadow of it}} (the vine); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=19|verse=23}}. So also some of the examples in {{GHGpar|116|k}} of passive participles of these verbs, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=10}},<section end=par121 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
